overview: This bill directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO), Congress's nonpartisan auditing agency, to study how federal regulators handle applications for bank and credit union mergers. In particular, it would look at the commitments and conditions that regulators, including the Federal Reserve, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the FDIC and the National Credit Union Administration, attach to merger approvals, and whether those conditions match what the law requires or have been shaped by unrelated considerations. The study would also weigh the effects of merger reviews on safety, financial stability, competition and access to financial services. A report would be due within one year. As of February 25, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say banks deserve clear, predictable merger reviews, and an independent study can show whether regulators have imposed conditions that go beyond what the law allows.
against: Critics say the study's framing suggests merger conditions are improper, which could pressure regulators to drop requirements meant to protect communities and competition when banks combine.
